_note: 4 shots, sparse. Mechanism: bad system. The all-staff email cascade — each person trying to stop it makes it worse. Ends on the narrator becoming part of the problem.

premise.situation: Someone replies all to a company-wide email asking to be removed from the list
premise.turn: Forty people reply all telling everyone to stop replying all
premise.detail: one person replies all with the single word 'unsubscribe'

character_sheet: a woman in her thirties, glasses, cardigan, sitting at an office desk

beats.text: Somebody replied all to four hundred people this morning.
To ask to be taken off the list. Which is a reasonable thing to want.
Then someone replied all to say please stop replying all.
Then eleven more people replied all to agree with him.
One man simply wrote the word unsubscribe. To four hundred people.
I have watched this happen for two hours and done nothing.
I am not on that list. I have no idea whose emails these are.

shots.prompt: close up of a computer monitor showing a wall of dense unreadable email rows stacking up, blue screen glow on a dim desk
wide shot of a huge open plan office where every single person is staring at their own screen with the same tense expression
extreme close up of a single finger pressing an oversized send key on a keyboard, dramatic hard light
medium shot of a woman sitting alone at a desk lit only by her monitor, watching intently, faintly delighted, chin on hand
